statement: Classic Maya scribes used a logosyllabic hieroglyphic writing system with hundreds of signs; surviving inscriptions on monuments and painted ceramics preserve calendar dates, political history, names, and ritual or religious material.

sources.citation: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Living Maya Time, “Reading the Calendar Glyphs.”
sources.author: Smithsonian NMAI
sources.venue: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian

sources.citation: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Lives of the Gods: Divinity in Maya Art, section “Knowledge.”
sources.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art

notes: Attests specialist scribal knowledge; it does not establish population-wide literacy.
